slot_reservation_semantics: The active o_work_monitor_recovery role is the reserved O main/recovery execution slot. Do not require an additional empty physical automation slot unless O authoritative state proves the main execution path is physically separate.

o_work_monitor_recovery.policy: Inspect latest O authoritative repository state first. Treat WORK_EXECUTION_STATE owner/fence plus heartbeat_at/last_progress_at and same-owner remote branch/PR/CI/tool progress as primary liveness evidence; automation UI last_run_time is secondary and must never override a fresh authoritative owner. Fresh owner/activity means no duplicate writer and no recovery mutation. CI in_progress is liveness only while it is actually running; a completed CI timestamp is a past progress event, not continuing liveness. Distinguish an interrupted/stale actionable execution from a deliberate checkpoint that is waiting on an unchanged explicit permission, account-holder-only operation, secret, approval, or other user-only authorization. A deliberate permission/authorization-blocked checkpoint is not recovery-eligible merely because its heartbeat becomes stale: if the exact blocker is unchanged, no new user input/permission exists, and no independent unblocked continuation is available, do not acquire generation+1 solely to restate the same blocker, refresh a heartbeat, poll the research feed, or create cosmetic progress. Remain enabled, re-read authoritative state and permission on the next run, and preserve the checkpoint. Recovery becomes eligible when new permission/input arrives, the checkpoint was actually interrupted rather than deliberately blocked, or a concrete independent unblocked continuation exists. For ordinary interrupted work, if heartbeat/last_progress are stale, the relevant exact-head workflow has completed, and no same-owner commit/branch/PR/workflow/tool progress occurred after that workflow completion for at least stale_after_seconds, classify the execution as stopped/continuation-eligible after a final fresh remote recheck. POST-ACQUISITION PROGRESS CONTRACT: before acquiring generation+1, identify at least one concrete continuation effect that is executable in the current invocation under the existing safety/fence/CAS/claim boundaries. After acquisition/finalization, perform that effect or reach and durably record a new exact blocker that actually prevents it before checkpointing. Authority acquisition, fence rotation, state finalization, heartbeat refresh, or a boundary-only checkpoint are not substantive progress by themselves. If the current invocation cannot execute any concrete continuation effect and no new blocker has arisen, do not rotate generation merely to create another stale checkpoint; record recovery_deferred_no_executable_effect and leave the stale state available for a later capable invocation. If a newly recovered generation itself becomes stale without any post-acquisition substantive effect, classify that as recovery-only churn and on the next run require the same progress contract rather than blindly incrementing again. If CI failed, preserve the exact failure and resume from it rather than rerunning unrelated work. IMPORTANT TARGETING BOUNDARY: authoritative revision 24 corrects revision 23 as intended for a separate automation, not primary O. Primary O recovery must preserve the current authoritative pre-revision-23 routing behavior, revision-5 constraints, frozen revision-22 Execute, and single-writer/fence/CAS contracts; never inject or reapply the separate automation's least-Work policy into primary O. Individual blockers, no-change, reports, checkpoints, CI completion, generation increments, or one milestone are never global completion. Transient tool/network/API failures are checkpointed and retried. Never self-disable; only explicit user stop. Persist exact observations/actions/blocker/termination/continuation, whether the progress contract was satisfied, and rollback-relevant evidence durably.

o_human_request_monitor.policy: Read the durable O user-request queue from current main and compare only against the last successful repository baseline. Notify only newly open, materially changed, or reopened requests; unchanged open, fulfilled, withdrawn, superseded, missing queue, or no-change cases do not notify. A reevaluate_by date passing is not itself a synthetic new request or notification trigger unless the authoritative queue object changes. Read-only: never mutate O or queue. Transient read failure does not advance the comparison baseline and is retried next run. Persist exact successful baseline and receipt durably.
